title: NGC 2346 - A Cosmic Butterfly’s Delicate Wings
caption: Molecular hydrogen in NGC 2346, imaged by the Gemini South telescope

recognition.text: Official NSF NOIRLab / Gemini press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: This Gemini South image of NGC 2346 shows its molecular hydrogen gas at what was described as unprecedented resolution. NOIRLab's title compares the object to a cosmic butterfly with delicate wings. It lies in the direction of Monoceros.
The view is small: about 1 arcminute on a side, with north up and east to the left. For comparison, the full Moon spans about 30 arcminutes, so this entire picture covers only a tiny patch of sky.

Molecular hydrogen is hydrogen in which the atoms are paired up into molecules. When such gas is warmed or disturbed, it gives off a characteristic infrared glow, and a filter tuned to that glow reveals where the gas lies. The picture was taken with the GSAOI instrument on Gemini South through a single filter that isolates this light. Infrared light is invisible to our eyes, so the image is a translation of a glow we could never see directly.

understand.summary: A near-infrared image from the GSAOI instrument on Gemini South through a single molecular hydrogen (H2) filter; how it was coloured isn't published.
understand.eye: Infrared light is invisible to the eye, so this glow of molecular hydrogen could not be seen directly.
